_doc: Nesting-habitat rules (cliff-nesters) shared by lib/habitat.py and viewer/habitat.js; tests/parity.py keeps the JS copy in step. Metres on the 1 m grid, degrees with 0 = north clockwise.
_doc.STEEP_DEG: a 1 m pixel this steep (degrees) counts as cliff
_doc.SMOOTH_M: the DTM is smoothed by this sigma (m) before slopes: one odd pixel (a road edge) cannot win
_doc.MIN_AREA: m2: smaller steep specks are not drawn
_doc.NEAR_R: m: polygons + steepest point within this of the centre (viz3d sets it to the view's radius)
_doc.CLIFF_MIN_H: m: a nesting cliff's face is at least this high
_doc.HIGH_FACE_M: m: a face at least this high is a 'high face' (one point of fit)
_doc.FACING: degrees [from, to]: only faces looking E ... S ... W count - more sun, less snow in the breeding season
_doc.PREF_FACING: degrees [from, to]: the preferred, sun-facing band SE ... S ... SW (one point of fit)
_doc.VERTICAL_DEG: degrees: a pixel at least this steep is near-vertical (the face's vertical share)
_doc.FACE_PAD_M: m: the face plus this much round it gives its top and foot (grey dilation 2*pad+1, binary dilation pad)
_doc.DROP_HALF_M: m: the sharpest step = height range within +-this (max - min filter of size 2*half+1)
_doc.ISLET_MAX_HA: ha: islands this small (inside the read square) are ground-nest islets
_doc.ISLET_MIN_M2: m2: smaller islands (and islet polygons) are left out
_doc.SEA_LEVEL_M: m: the 1 m model fills the sea with ~0 m; ground at or below this is sea
_doc.NEAR_BUILDING: m: a cliff closer than this to a building is less suitable
_doc.NEAR_ROAD: m: a cliff closer than this to a road is less suitable
_doc.EDGE_M: m: nothing is detected this close to the data's edge (the view's border, a missing tile)
_doc.SIMPLIFY_CLIFF_M: m: Douglas-Peucker tolerance of the cliff polygons
_doc.SIMPLIFY_ISLET_M: m: Douglas-Peucker tolerance of the islet polygons
_doc.COLOURS: fill by kind (quarry, islet) and, as a fallback, by fit score 1..3
_doc.FACE_COLOURS: cliff fill by facing: S strongest, SE / SW orange, E / W pale
_doc.TITLE: the habitat layer's title
